newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil close to ending PROER bank credit program.
newsitem.headline: Brazil close to ending PROER bank credit program.

text.p: Brazil is ready to end its PROER program to encourage mergers and acquistions in the country's private banking sector, Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said Wednesday.
"We can comfortably say that the transition process is complete. Of course there will still be transition in the public banks," Loyola told a news conference.
"The moment has come to consider the end of PROER. That is a question we will be studying and there will be an announcement soon," he said.

PROER was set up in November 1995 to aid the takeover of failed bank Banco Nacional by Banco Economico. Since then, the program has been used to help the acquisition of several banks struggling to adapt to a low-inflation environment. A total of about 20 billion reais in credit has been issued under PROER.
Loyola said the restructuring of Brazil's publicly owned banks had only just begun and that the privatization last week of Banerj, a bank owned by Rio de Janeiro state, was "an important step."
He said the process would continue with the upcoming selloff of Credireal, a bank owned by Minas Gerais state.
